overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals clear audience preference for space, extreme planetary conditions, and 'What If' hypothetical scenarios, particularly when framed with high-stakes curiosity. Videos published in late September and early October (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') significantly outperform older psychology or standard animal facts on views-per-day and likes-per-view metrics. Conversely, simple biological facts and older historical/psychological tricks show low relative engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views in ~3 weeks) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) demonstrate high velocity and strong like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-stakes hypothetical planetary survival or entry scenarios using vivid, tactile descriptions (melting, crushing, freezing).

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring counter-intuitive planetary physics or extreme environments like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views in 2 weeks) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,027 views) perform exceptionally well.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on lesser-known exoplanets and cosmic phenomena that challenge human intuition about time, light, and physics.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) show stagnant growth and low engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard self-help or basic neuroscience facts unless framed through an extreme, bizarre narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' have plateaued in daily view velocity compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal-related content into cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric scenarios rather than simple listicle facts.

next_video.concept: Stepping foot on a rogue planet drifting through interstellar space with no star.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with the terrifying pitch: imagine walking on a world that hasn't seen sunlight in 4 billion years.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite the pitch-black freezing surface, an underground ocean of liquid nitrogen or water could harbor bizarre life.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary exploration format while introducing a fresh astronomical subject (rogue planets) not yet covered in the channel's history.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature black holes, diamond planets, burning ice planets, or Saturn.
Must focus strictly on rogue wandering planets.
Must maintain factual accuracy regarding interstellar space physics.

experiment: Test a 15-second pacing structure on a rogue planet 'What If' scenario to determine if shorter duration improves retention compared to the 21-second top performers.
